title: Probably: Guessing With the Future and the Conditional

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *estará* and *serían* from B1 Unit 22: the future can be a guess about the present (*Estará en casa*: "He is probably at home") and the conditional a guess about the past (*Serían las ocho cuando llegó el tren*: "It was probably about eight"). You use them when you do not know a fact and say what seems likely: when a film starts, how long it lasts, who is at the cinema.

items.spanish: Mi amiga no contesta; estará en el cine.
items.english: My friend is not answering; she is probably at the cinema.

items.spanish: No sé cuánto dura la película; durará unas dos horas.
items.english: I do not know how long the film is; it probably lasts about two hours.

items.spanish: Serán las nueve, porque ya hay mucha gente en la sala.
items.english: It is probably nine o'clock, because there are already many people in the theatre.

items.spanish: Serían las diez cuando terminó la película.
items.english: It was probably about ten when the film ended.

sections.content: Do not use these forms for facts you know. *Roma es de 2018* is a fact; *Roma será de 2018* would mean "it is probably from 2018". The conditional guesses about the past: use it with a past event, as in *Serían las diez cuando terminó*.
